turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Howzit. Have a seat. What's the problem today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, sorry, the robot by the mall was a mess. It's my ear though. Ringing, in the right one.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): A month. And it's worse when it's quiet, hey, especially when I'm lying there trying to sleep.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Is it a tumour? I googled last night. Eish, I shouldn't have.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pain?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No pain.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any discharge?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing coming out.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dizzy? Room spinning?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not dizzy. The hearing's gone a bit muffled though, like cotton wool in that ear.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Am I going deaf? Just tell me straight, doc.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Can't say that. No hearing test for now. Come back in six weeks if the ringing's still there.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Six weeks? He stands on the grinder the whole day at the panel shop. Never puts the plugs in.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Loud machinery, and no ear protection?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Grinders, compressor, the lot. Plugs sit in the bakkie. They itch, so I leave them.
[SEG0017] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the TV is so loud I have to shout from the kitchen. He reckons he can't hear it otherwise.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): Muffling just on the right?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, the right. Left is fine, I think. Is the left going to start as well?
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No headaches.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): I've had a look. Right drum is clear, no wax. Left is the same.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Not wax then? So what is it actually doing in there?
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pressure today is one thirty eight over eighty four. Pulse seventy six.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that high? Maybe the ringing is from the pressure. Is my tablet even working?
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pressure's fine. What are you taking, and the doses?

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, amlodopine for the pressure, ten milligram, uh no, five milligram, in the morning. The cholesterol one at night, I always forget the name, twenty milligram. And sugar tablets, two of them with breakfast, white round ones, I don't know the proper name.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh and only the aryuvedic powder in the morning, a teaspoon, from the shop. Does that clash with the tablets?
[SEG0029] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He doesn't skip that powder. Every single morning, ja.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Forget the six weeks. That plan's out.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): With the noise and no plugs, I'm referring you for a hearing test at audiology.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Is the test sore? Needles? How long does it even take?
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): No needles. Headphones and beeps. Half an hour, more or less.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): And if the hearing's bad, can I still work? We can't have me sitting at home.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): You carry on working. Ear plugs in every shift, from tomorrow. Itch or not.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): What if the ringing gets really bad while I wait? Must I stop the powder? I paid a lot for that tin.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Don't stop your tablets, and I'm not changing the powder today. If the hearing suddenly drops, or you start spinning, or one side goes weak, come straight in.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. Ok. Shame, I just keep thinking it's something bad.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Most likely it's noise-related ringing. I won't know the hearing properly until that test.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): So not a tumour? You're sure?
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm not calling it a tumour. I'll see you in three weeks with the result. Get the audiology slip from reception on your way out.
[SEG0042] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Come. The meter's running on the bakkie, and you've asked enough, hey.

spec.situation: Ringing in the right ear for a month, worse in quiet; works with loud machinery without ear protection; some muffled hearing; hearing test referral.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

bad.reason: Muffled hearing in right ear is supported; severity 'mild' is not stated.
bad.text: Muffled hearing (category=ENT, status=present, severity=mild, temporality=current, body_site=right ear, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Diabetes/"sugar" treated with tablets is present in the history (patient takes sugar tablets with breakfast).
Muffled hearing is only on the right; patient said the left ear is fine. Laterality of unilateral hearing change was explicitly discussed.
Doctor initially said 'come back in six weeks if the ringing is still there' and then explicitly reversed that plan ('Forget the six weeks. That plan's out'). This change of plan is not captured.
Patient expressed uncertainty about the amlodipine dose, first saying 10 mg and then correcting to 5 mg.
